newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dips again in nervous, choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dips again in nervous, choppy trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude was narrowly weaker in choppy afternoon trade on Thursday as bearish fundamentals held a slight advantage over supportive technical factors, dealers said.
Prompt March Brent, which expires at the close, dipped to a new session low of $20.42 a barrel. By 1530 GMT it had recovered slightly to $20.45, still seven cents off Wednesday's close.
The more actively traded April Brent shed six cents to $20.18.
"It's pretty nervous today. People aren't sure about which way it's going to go next," said a broker.

"There's been a bit of fund selling coming in this afternoon but March volumes are pretty light and the open interest is not so huge which suggests a lot of people have already got out," said a broker.

A deteriorating fundamental picture of waning demand in the traditional lull between the winter heating oil and spring gasoline seasons, rising supply and talk of extra Iraqi exports held the upper hand, brokers said.
"With global supply from both OPEC and non-OPEC on the rise, fundamentals just don't look too good at the moment," said brokers GNI in a daily report.

Some brokers who follow technical charts noted, however, that stochastics and relative strength indices (RSIs) were looking increasingly oversold and the market could be due for a modest correction after shedding $2 a barrel this month.
"All is not black - we have numerous gaps above and are getting oversold with stochastics looking supportive," said Charles Gray of brokers Prudential-Bache's energy desk.
Meanwhile, March gas oil shed $4.50 to $180.00 a tonne by 1550 GMT.
